# Stock Wide `Array(T)` numeric fixture

Generated by `scripts/generate_array_numeric_fixture.sh` with the pinned
ClickHouse 26.7.1.1315 official build in a disposable local store. The captured
part contains `pk UInt64` plus one `Array(T)` column for each of `UInt8`,
`UInt16`, `UInt32`, `UInt64`, `Int8`, `Int16`, `Int32`, `Int64`, `Float32`,
and `Float64`. The source insert is RowBinary, and floating-point inputs are
specified as raw IEEE-754 bit patterns so signed zero and NaN payloads do not
depend on text parsing. Generation runs `CHECK TABLE`; the bidirectional oracle
attaches the captured part to stock ClickHouse and checks it again.

All columns use the same seven keys: `1, 2, 4, 6, 9, 11, 13`. Every array is
empty for keys 1, 4, and 13. In particular, key 4 is an empty middle row between
non-empty arrays at keys 2 and 6; keys 4 and 6 share a mark, and the final mark
contains the empty key 13. This checks that per-row lengths and following leaf
values stay associated with the correct outer rows. The raw `<column>.size0`
stream stores per-row lengths `[0, 2, 0, 2, 2, 1, 0]` for each numeric leaf.
Granularity is two rows, producing mark rows `[2, 2, 2, 1]` and a short final
mark. The fixture uses a forced Wide part, LZ4 data, uncompressed plain `.mrk2`
marks, and 4 KiB maximum decompression blocks.

The physical streams per array are exactly `<column>.size0` and `<column>`;
there is no nullable bitmap because the admitted W30 shape is plain `Array(T)`.
The primitive edge rows cover zero and each integer type's min/max encodings.
Float32 uses `-0` (`0x80000000`), `+0`, quiet NaN payload `0x7fc12345`, max
finite, `+Inf`, `-max finite`, `-Inf`, `1.5`, `-2.25`, and both signed minimum
subnormals. Float64 uses the corresponding encodings, with NaN payload
`0x7ff8000000001234`.

`SHA256SUMS` pins every captured part file. This fixture certifies only this
producer build and the listed one-level numeric-array shapes; it does not
certify nullable leaves or arbitrary array compositions.
